submission.natural_language_explanation: The direction fires most strongly on a space-minus token ' -' used as a unary negative sign directly before a number, when it follows an operator or slot opener ('- -4', '+ -5', '/ -5', '= -3', ': -1', ', -2', 'to -40'); a binary subtraction minus ('7 - 5', 'a - b') stays at zero. A weaker, secondary component fires on the closing subword piece of a multi-token technical or biomedical word (alkylid|ene, carben|es, Pancre|atic, D-d|imer, lig|ament) and on the verb ' miss'.

rival_explanations: Broader: the direction fires on any ' -' token in a numeric context, including binary subtraction between two numbers or variables ('7 - 5', 'a - b'), not only on negative signs.

Different main job: the direction mainly marks the completing subword of multi-token rare or technical words (chemistry, anatomy, medicine), and the negative-sign firings are an incidental case of a token that completes a '- -N' or '= -N' unit.
